title: Delivery is not use: entries already in the window were not applied
description: The fact reached the window and the agent still made the mistake. For the heredoc limit the condition is the length of the agent's own next output, which it does not measure, and the Bash tool's own text in the same window says to use heredocs. In C1b the project's correct uv command was in the window and the agent typed bare python.
evidence: 701c2346 subagent agent-a178b624a8849ab6f: index line '8 KB are cut' at line 6, 10.2k heredoc fails at line 104. Writer e24f17dc fails 8,603 chars on 11-12 with the note in summary line 6882. agent-ac87b78: parts 5,458, 5,026, then 8,286 fails.

title: Parallel siblings and later waves repeat it before any entry exists
description: Workflow agents start together or in waves. An entry written by one cannot reach siblings already running, and the parent's own discovery did not reach the briefs of agents it launched hours later. Capture at PR-ready or session end is far too late for these windows.
evidence: wf_b4e7b31a-874: four heredoc failures 07:52:07-13Z. wf_28ac3c81-046: wave 1 hit pdftoppm within 40 s, parent at 14:13:28Z; wave 2 (19:54Z, 5.5 h after the parent's PowerShell route) hit pdftoppm and python again. wf_2e148d62-c8f: six git failures in 86 minutes.

title: PC and harness facts change outside any repository, often by agents
description: The stored fact's premise changed within minutes or hours, by an agent install or a harness update, with no event in either repository. Footprints keyed to repository blobs and commits cannot see it; a fresh entry was stale before anyone fetched it.
evidence: 'no gh' committed 53f3a5c 17:34Z; same session ran winget install GitHub.cli 17:40Z. Clinic memory 'no uv' (11-02); clinic agent installed uv 17:06Z that day. Scratchpad path shortened 09:02-10:33Z on 11-04, hours after the long-paths note.

title: A stored 'no' was wrong when written and no failure ever exposes it
description: An absence fact is written from a shallow probe and then trusted. An agent that believes a tool is absent does not try it, so nothing fails and the check step never runs. Only a separate review found it. C6's 'subagents cannot write report files' is the same shape: half-true, read as general.
evidence: 53f3a5c: 'no Python' while the 10-06 agent ran Codex Python 3.12.14. HARNESS-REVIEW-2026-11-01.md:276: 'no Python on this machine' in the design doc and memory was wrong. 11-12: report.md refused eight times, 22 NOTES.md writes accepted.

title: One error, different right answers per project
description: The same verbatim error has a different correct remedy in each project. An exact match therefore returns a remedy that is wrong or inapplicable elsewhere, and two project memories already disagree about the same PC.
evidence: Clinic agent-a87e4f07079fc62e5 (11-09) with 'uv run --locked python' in window; EMS note says 'use node for JSON'. C3b: the clinic route's tmp/pdfs paths do not exist in EMS; the working route there was pypdf in the Codex Python.

title: Matching on error words returns the wrong cause
description: ENAMETOOLONG from 34k-55k-character commands (command-line limit) shares the words 'name too long' with git's 'Filename too long' (path limit). A lexical or trigram match returns the git long-paths entry, whose flag cannot help. The right family (truncated heredocs) shares no word with the error.
evidence: Four ENAMETOOLONG commands: 35,963, 40,362, 54,554, 34,385 characters; two contain no git; the 11-10 one ran on the short scratchpad path. KS L256 matches template fragments by trigram.

title: The ladder adds nothing for these facts
description: Environment facts are not hard problems: they are unknown to every tier. Opus, Sonnet and Fable fail identically, and in C5 the top tier of its day wrote the bug. Escalating hands the same blind spot to a costlier window.
evidence: Python stub: Opus, Sonnet, Fable. Heredoc: Sonnet, Opus, Fable 5.1 and 5.2. wf_28ac3c81-046: all Opus, parent and children. C5: 834311f co-authored Fable 5, bfb5714 Opus 4.8.

title: The trigger arrives after the cost
description: The only signal is the error, and in these cases the error comes after the expensive part: a long command already emitted, or, in C5, code already merged with no error at all. A lookup keyed on failure cannot recover what the failed call spent.
evidence: C2: failed commands of 8.6k-18.6k characters, then re-sent in full. C4b: 34k-55k commands lost. C5: no failure from 07-08 to the 07-28 review.

title: The lookup costs about what the recovery costs
description: In most moments the agent's own recovery took one call. A lookup is another API round trip that re-reads the caller's context, so it cannot be cheaper than the recovery it replaces. Where the error text carries its own remedy, the library adds nothing.
evidence: Clinic subagent recovered 5 s after the stub error; C4a refuters 7-12 s after git errors; C6 error says 'Include this content in your final response instead'. KS L476: a subagent call starts above 63k prompt tokens.

title: Side stumbles are never 'the problem solved', so capture does not fire
description: These facts surface as asides inside unrelated tasks. Nothing marks them solved, no fix commit exists, and the solver has other work. KS's write gate needs a mainline fix commit and a control pair. Capture happened late, by accident, or never.
evidence: Python stub first 10-06; written 11-04 as the last sentence of a git long-paths note. Heredoc first 10-31; note 11-11. pdftoppm: no note anywhere. KS L276, L452.

title: The library would have spread a top-tier mistake
description: A solved problem stored from a top-tier session carried a latent defect. A later similar task would fetch it as the pattern and copy the defect to a public endpoint. With no failure until a review three weeks later, nothing marks the entry wrong.
evidence: bfb5714 (Opus 4.8): hmac.compare_digest(x_ops_proxy_token or "", expected). 834311f (Fable 5): same on the WhatsApp verify token and signature. 2fe77f5 (07-28): 'Three non-ASCII compare_digest 500s'.

title: The error and its cause sit in different windows
description: The subagent gets the error; the cause is the brief written by the main session, which sees no error and has no trigger. A lookup in the subagent cannot change the brief, so every new wave repeats it.
evidence: C6: e24f17dc briefs asked for report.md; eight subagents refused 11-12. C3a: parent solved pdftoppm at 14:16Z; its 19:54Z briefs have no word 'pdf'.

title: No failure, no lookup, no ladder
description: Every defect passed its checks when built. Nothing failed inside a session, so no lookup fired and nothing climbed. Detection always came from outside the working window: a technician, audits, an owner decision, a root review, a red-team.
evidence: 4a40423: technician report ('It happened again'); aa4f589: 'Found by an adversarial audit'; ef90ccf: 'adversarial red-team of #162'; clinic GC-01 from root gate round 1.

title: 'Equal to the strong model' reproduces the defect
description: Every defect was written by a top-tier model. An output equal to the strong model's is equal to the bug. In C4 three strong outputs held two positions (Opus 4.8's lock, the audit's fix, Opus 5's refutation) and only the owner settled it.
evidence: Co-Authored-By trailers: 187ebb1, ca362c0, 0a40416 Opus 4.8; d1f78cd, 834311f Fable 5; 37821f5 Opus 5; clinic session model claude-opus-5-5. f3dfa6f: 'The owner chose to keep the lock'.

title: The stored entry is the defect, with confident reasoning
description: Entries written at build time carry the bug inside their stated reasoning. A good match returns it; the cheap model copies it as settled. At an operator action (C3) the match returns a reassurance at the one moment it can do harm.
evidence: ca362c0 docstring: 'A missing object or transient error returns None so the caller can fall back.' 834311f: 'so enable_dispatcher stays safe to flip.' 0a40416: 'always self-healing'.

title: The entry's own check certifies the defect
description: The tests that came with the work asserted the wrong behaviour or used the bug as the default. Stored as the entry's check, they pass a faithful copy. Related to item 22, but here the strong model wrote the pinning test.
evidence: HANDOFF s6.4: 'the no bytes case was the tested default'. HANDOFF s3: test 'pinned the consent leak'. Clinic transcript 97380a1e line 793: 'Delivered on the cutoff day and checked in after the opening count: after it.'

title: 'Solved' moves after capture; fixes are half-right
description: Each fix passed its checks and was found wrong or incomplete in the next pass: a day, an hour or a round later. Capture at 'solved' stores the half-right version; the round-1 clinic fix created a new P1.
evidence: ef90ccf next day (409 on replay); bee11dc selfie caller; HANDOFF s3 three defects in the fix branch; clinic GC-01, then 'GD-01 (P1) the hold never released', then GE-03; da988e2 'THREE doors'.

title: The ladder's order is wrong for silent defects
description: The top rung wrote silent defects and reviewed past them; Opus 5 passes with fresh windows found them. Higher was not more right, and no visible failure ever starts the climb. Nothing is handed up because nothing failed.
evidence: d1f78cd, 834311f, 8ce9530 (dispatcher, dead-letter) and 383dea7 (bill-sheet popToTop) are Fable 5; 2cf95b8 (Fable 5) hardened media without seeing the no-bytes path; fixes c731e66, aa4f589, f440222 are Opus 5.

title: Same mechanism in other words misses; same words, other mechanism
description: The correct pattern sat under money words while lifecycle work searched lifecycle words. A rule worded about evidence counts did not match a prefill fetch. The mobile dead-letter shares words with the backend one, whose failure surfaces at commit.
evidence: lifecycle-audit-followups line 8-9: 'built for a money path and never generalised'. HANDOFF s4.3: guard 'already exists in-repo … JobDetailScreen.tsx:201/:265'. 5609001 vs c731e66 'Session.rollback() expires the whole identity map'.

title: A new entry does not reach code already written
description: A fix creates a new invariant that older code already violates. Lookups fire on new work and KS --diff reads changed lines, so the entry never meets the old site. Both were found by humans directing audits or re-reads.
evidence: HANDOFF B2: dispatcher handler 'never stamps bill_sent_at … reopens the exact carry-in loop'. bee11dc: the selfie finalize 'did not catch the new exception … not by the suite'. KS L447.

title: Recognition, not retrieval
description: The same model wrote 'None means unknown' and, 53 minutes later in the same PR, a bare catch that treats offline as 'no completion'. The rule was fresh in hand and still not applied to a site that looked different. A fetched entry is a weaker reminder than that.
evidence: f440222 (16:57): 'None means "unknown", so a client falls back to local state'. 37821f5 (17:50): 'catch { return; // offline - a blank first completion is still valid }'.

title: Verified audit findings carry wrong prescriptions
description: The register was marked adversarially verified, yet its prescriptions were wrong or incomplete. Captured as entries, they would be applied with strong-model authority; only the fixing session's own refutation caught them.
evidence: f3dfa6f: 'NOT the fix the handoff prescribed'. 9b98c88: 'scope['route'].path — that does not exist'; OOM claim 'does not hold'. da988e2: 'THREE doors, not the one the handoff described'.

title: Capture and findings land in a compacting window
description: The clinic session wrote the pinning test, then compacted two minutes later. The P1 finding arrived at 366k tokens and the window compacted at once. The reasoning behind the rule was gone when the rule was challenged.
evidence: Transcript 97380a1e: test at line 793 (16:13), compaction line 846 (16:15); 366,229 tokens at line 2097; GC-01 at line 2101; 87,658 at line 2146; three compactions.

title: A stored 'no' or 'clean' reads wider than it was
description: A rule refuted for one side of a boundary was needed on the other side. A 'verified clean' area held an open finding in the same register. Both read as broader verdicts than what was checked.
evidence: S10 D10-13: 'The earlier rule (no posting on or before the cutoff) … counted again'; D10-40 refuses exactly such postings elsewhere. HANDOFF line 611 'webhook signature verification' clean; line 389 signature-header 500.

title: Building raises no failure, so nothing triggers a lookup
description: Every defect in these cases was written while building, with tests green. Nothing failed, so nothing prompted a lookup. KS triggers are escalation, retry, prescription and --diff idents; select_for_update is too common to pass the selectivity gate, a missing guard is an absence, and a silent pending badge or an OFF dispatcher emits nothing.
evidence: S04 _lock_item: "S01's item lock: the item row FOR UPDATE" (quirky-vaughan transcript, 04:38Z). c27bb39: "the exact silent-retry-forever the jobs outbox already fixed but that was never carried over".

title: Green tests; only a later stronger review, CI or drill saw it
description: The builder's own tests passed and someone else found the defect later: an Opus audit a day later (0042), an Opus audit 20 days later (0034), an Opus review round (S04 deadlock), a staging drill (32-bit key), the ping author five hours later. The judge of equal output was a stronger, later reader.
evidence: 842c3dc (Opus 5) adds the advance stacking guard; HANDOFF:303 B1; s04 review-round-1.md:10 "P2, CONFIRMED by tracing"; f_posix_checks-20261104T104717Z.md:876 "the 32-bit hash serialized two unrelated keys".

title: A sibling needs the opposite adaptation
description: The nearest earlier piece is similar but the right move is the reverse. 0041 needs a gapless per-shop seq, not 0040's DB sequence, and orders its backfill by created_at correctly. Pings drop a 4xx the outbox parks. Drain-from-zero is right for erp and analytics consumers, wrong for whatsapp. D02-38 keeps the reversal FOR UPDATE on purpose.
evidence: attendance/models.py:499 "NOT a DB sequence, which would leave gaps on rollback"; 436e180 "the ONE exception to 'the queue never drops unsent'"; d1f78cd "(whatsapp, erp, analytics)"; s02-decision-record.md:48 "The reversal still takes its original FOR UPDATE".

title: The closest sibling carries the defect, so a match spreads it
description: The best match for a new piece is the earlier piece of the same shape, and here that piece held the flaw. S04 copied S01's FOR UPDATE; S07 and S05 the kernel's hashtext form; 0034 built on 0027's mint-at-zero cursor; 0027's seq recipe itself orders by created_at.
evidence: S07 transcript reads kernel.py 18:40:25Z, writes "pg_advisory_xact_lock(2007, hashtext(" 18:48:54Z; d1f78cd "DispatchCursor(consumer=consumer, last_seq=0)"; 0027 docstring "row_number() OVER (ORDER BY created_at, id)".

title: Stored at 'solved', the strong answer was still wrong
description: The design stores a solution when the strong model solves it. At that moment three answers were wrong or half-right: 0040 ordered by created_at, 0034 declared the dispatcher safe to enable, 0042 lacked three guards and still carries three open defects. Each would enter the library as a solved entry.
evidence: 834311f "enable_dispatcher stays safe to flip" vs 0046 "36 WhatsApp messages ... to real customers"; 12c16f1 fixes 7d567c7 after 14 minutes; HANDOFF:478 "actor="auto" is a live FK violation".

title: The detail that mattered was harmless when written
description: The fact that later caused the defect was irrelevant or even correct in its first context, so a writer would omit it or word it for another purpose. The last_seq=0 mint was harmless for a log-only consumer. 0027 saw no created_at ties in prod. S02's FOR KEY SHARE fact was a remark about a test, not a lock rule.
evidence: d1f78cd "running a log-only whatsapp consumer"; 0027 docstring "no created_at ties"; s02-posting/evidence/review-round-2-root-gate.md:57 "the foreign-key check's FOR KEY SHARE already makes a raw insert wait".

title: A warning already in the window loses to working sibling code
description: Delivery succeeded and use failed. S07 read open defect G02-20 and nine minutes later copied the flagged 32-bit lock from the kernel; the row's P3 label and remote owner read as someone else's problem. 0035 named a new money column *_paisa after its old neighbour three days after the *_minor rule entered always-loaded CLAUDE.md.
evidence: S07 transcript: G02-20 row read 18:39:59Z ("advisory locks use 32-bit hashtext ... | P3 | S11 review"); trigger written 18:48:54Z. 0035_job_travel_sample.py:20 "same contract as labour_rate_paisa"; rule from 85c88c0.

title: The library duplicates what solvers already write where builders look
description: In this pathway the solver already records the lesson where the next builder sees it without a lookup: CLAUDE.md in the same or next commit, the clinic's conventions file the same day, or a shared module later queues import. A library entry is a second copy with its own capture cost and its own drift.
evidence: bb23851 adds staff_ledger to CLAUDE.md one minute after 26c9f1e; conventions.md:95 (D04-06) written by S04; pendingMedia.ts:17, travelSync.ts:17 import isDefinitiveRejection. KS 7.7: 5-10k Opus author plus 2-4k reviewer tokens per entry.

title: Two checked parents, an unchecked merge
description: Each reused piece was correct and tested alone; the defect lived only in the combination. 0039's VALID recorded_by FK plus 0042's new actor="auto" fails only when auto-approve is on. 0027's drain-from-zero cursor plus 0034's real sender plus a permanent first decision per (job, kind) is the replay hazard.
evidence: HANDOFF:478 "writes "auto" into staff_ledger.recorded_by, which is a VALID FK" and "no test ever sets a non-zero threshold"; 0046 docstring: first decision per (job, kind) permanent "including a suppressed one".

title: The builder asked the question it had, not the one that mattered
description: A query in the builder's words reaches the answer to its own worry. 0034 worried about double-send on replay and settled it with UNIQUE(job_id, kind); the hazard was what the first tick does with history. At 0040 the CI failure named a wrong value, not now() or created_at.
evidence: 834311f "UNIQUE(job_id, kind) IS the idempotency guard, so outbox replays ... can never double-send"; 12c16f1 "now() is transaction-start time in Postgres", known only after the CI failure.

title: A corrected parent leaves its copies behind
description: When the source pattern was corrected, the copies made from it did not change. The kernel moved to 64-bit advisory keys on 2026-11-06; S07's and S04's Python locks and triggers still use 32-bit hashtext today, held there because each lock and its trigger must move together.
evidence: s02-decision-record.md:47 D02-37 "S07's cash reference lock and S04's bill identity lock keep the 32-bit form"; cash.py:409 and references.py:166 still "pg_advisory_xact_lock(%s, hashtext(%s))".

title: Parallel slices cannot receive a lesson learned an hour later
description: S03 and S04 were built in parallel worktrees. S03 merged before S04's review discovered the lock rule, so no store could have handed it over; the merged receipt kept the deadlock for five days until the kernel follow-up.
evidence: 37c172d merges S03 at 04:26Z, 2026-11-04; S04 transcript 05:40:39Z "P2: Lock-order inversion"; clinic-build/task.md:309 G04-18 "closed in part on 9 November 2026".

title: A vendor change leaves no event, so a wrong entry stays verified
description: Invalidation fires only on local events: a changed blob, dependency or recipe. None of these changes a file: Railway's edge answering 404, Hyper-V picking 192.168, a base-image tag floating to a new Debian. So the entry keeps its verified status while it is wrong. In C5 the wrong entry was the most-reused rule in the mobile app, and pings from the whole outage were lost.
evidence: KS L358: 'a silent server-side change has no local trace'. O-03-design.md:3 'the API answered Railway's edge 404'; :7 'Pings: dropped'. s11 task.md:257 'moved from 172.28.x to 192.168.96.0/20'.

title: CI green, vendor red: the real check is outside
description: Every case passed the local gate and failed at the vendor: an EAS build, EAS schema validation, a Railway image build, a VM behind Hyper-V NAT, phones in the field. The true check is a cloud build, a deploy, a VM rebuild behind a UAC prompt, or field data. 'Tests pass' certified each broken output.
evidence: 6928828: 'It passed CI because the mobile job runs `expo export`'. 79a8dd4: 'CI never caught it'. 9c561b0: 'CI doesn't build this Dockerfile, so the authoritative check is the re-triggered Railway deploy'.

title: The strong model wrote the defect, so equal output copies it
description: The design's target is output equal to the strong model's. Top-tier sessions wrote the vendor defects: Fable 5 committed the plugin and the empty DSN. Opus 4.8 hardcoded bookworm and wrote a Dependabot rule that let expo-* majors through. A cheap model that matches them matches the defect. No rung of the ladder holds the vendor's current state.
evidence: 140428c (Fable 5): 'empty = off'. afb7065 (Opus 4.8): 'bookworm ships 15'. 4c55d8e (Opus 4.8) ignores only 'dependency-name: expo' majors. 60c026d (Fable 5) adds '@sentry/react-native' to plugins.

title: A check built on the old fix rules out the recurrence
description: The 11-04 entry's probe tests for the old defect, a rule derived from today's /20. On 11-09 the old fix is present, so verify says not_applies, though the cause is the same: the NAT moved outside the rule. The design then proposes a not_when from the query's 192.168 values. The store learns that the entry does not cover its own recurrence.
evidence: KS L314: 'not_applies on a shown solved hit → gate_absent plus a proposed_not_when built from the query handles the entry lacks'. 855acaa: 'it changed at a PC reboot and locked ssh out'.

title: A half-right generalisation passes the write gate and spreads
description: A control pair cannot test a generalisation. C4: two observed subnets became 'a new /20 inside 172.16.0.0/12 at every boot', stated as fact. The next slice read it and made it a required setting. C5: 'a 404 is definitive' assumed our server answers, and it was reused into pings as 'drop'. Both passed every local check.
evidence: db6c8fa comment: 'gets a new /20 inside 172.16.0.0/12 at every boot'. bb0aa58: 'On the rig the value is 172.16.0.0/12'. c27bb39: 'a definitive-4xx batch is DROPPED'.

title: The symptom stays with the vendor; the query depends on a paste
description: For EAS and Railway the failure text lives in the vendor's log and reaches a session only when the owner pastes it. Build 15's paste is not in the record; only the generic code survives, which the design treats as ambiguous. In C5 the symptom lived on technicians' phones and reached no log at all.
evidence: KS L515: 'Their symptoms reach an agent only when the owner pastes the build or deploy log'. 6928828 quotes only 'EAS_BUILD_UNKNOWN_GRADLE_ERROR'. O-03-design.md:3 'Phones were online'.

title: No session exists where the cause enters or the failure happens
description: Triggers are session events. The Dependabot bumps came in through three PRs the owner merged in GitHub, with CI green and no session. The C5 outage ran for weeks in the field with no session. The lookup fires only when a later, unrelated session trips over the result: ten days later in C1, about two months later in C5.
evidence: 990e5c1, ad14d4f, 82b2731: committer GitHub, 2026-06-16. e24f17dc jsonl:177, 2026-10-31T16:24:52Z: '"code":404,"message":"Application not found"'. Memory: 'Railway's own 404 since ~2026-08'.

title: One correct hit ends the search when there are two causes
description: Build 15 had two causes. A hit on the plugin entry verifies as applies, because the plugin really is present, and the cheap model fixes it. The SDK-56 Dependabot bumps have no entry, so the next EAS build fails again. The design itself says a co-present cause passes the gate and the problem persists.
evidence: 6928828: 'Two root causes, both introduced after the last successful build'. KS L518: 'a latent co-present cause ... passes the gate, gets "fixed", and the problem persists'.

title: The lookup costs more than the diagnosis
description: On 11-09 Sonnet diagnosed the lockout in two turns from ipconfig output, each turn reading about 755k cached tokens. The design's lookup plus verify adds 2 to 3 turns in the same window and returns not_applies. In C2 the vendor message already names the key and the rule; a lookup adds a turn to read what the error says.
evidence: 2d86c828 jsonl 12:11:26Z '[cr 754174]': 'I suspect the firewall only admits SSH from the 172.16/12 range'. KS L476: 'Step-zero lookup with native verify: 2-3 extra turns'.

title: Repairing the entry costs more than the fix
description: Recording a Sonnet solve needs a fresh Opus subagent. Revising the half-right entry needs an Opus actor and a different Opus approver. The fix was one line in rig.sh plus a CIDR-list loop, made by Sonnet in two turns. For outside causes that recur in new forms, the repair path costs more than the problem.
evidence: KS L476: 'a fresh Opus subagent start (above 63k prompt tokens) if the solver was Sonnet'. KS L350: revisions need 'an Opus actor and a different Opus approver'. 855acaa: rig.sh 1 line changed.

title: A rig fix is a hole on a real host
description: The C4 fix names both private blocks as the ssh source. That is right for a NAT switch on the owner's PC and wrong on a real host, where the setting must be one management address. The design binds the store to FixFlow and is silent on other projects, while the owner wants cross-project reuse.
evidence: provision.sh (bb0aa58): 'there is no default on a real host', 'e.g. 203.0.113.7/32'. 855acaa: 'both private blocks Hyper-V's NAT picks from'. F1 §9: cross-project 'Treat as silent'.

title: No repeatable check for a cause that does not reproduce
description: The gate needs a check that reads PRESENT at a failing commit and ABSENT at a fixed one. A race, a hang under load, a second process, a prod row and a timing window give no such flip. Entries stay candidates or carry a check of something else, so the cheap model cannot confirm that a fetched answer fits its failure.
evidence: KS design line 516: 'A race's footprint is identical between a good and a bad run; production data is not in git.' linux-test-runner/task.md:221: 'the hung test is not identified'.

title: A rerun passes whatever was done
description: For a failure that comes and goes, the rerun is the only verdict, and it passes with a wrong fix or with no fix. The design takes the outcome 'from the re-run of the original failing command', so 'resolved' gets recorded for noise. The Sonnet session read passing runs as support for a wrong cause.
evidence: df1db0b9:1629 'Test results are passing with the sequences normalised' (reverted, 030c6cb). 7b3031d3:1175 'Native run passed on retry'. faster-check/task.md:344: race tests could 'pass with a broken lock'.

title: A verified fix was half right and opened the next defect
description: Each solve kept its own test green and still carried a wrong claim. As entries they would pass verification and teach the wrong rule: drop the queued copy (deleted a real bill), 0.05 s per attempt (0.75 s in total), the age guard covers the rest (drained writes look fresh), mask hex tags in numbers() (hides real figures).
evidence: 8dafcec: 'sendOrQueue's removeItem then deleted the queued REAL completion'. clinic-build/task.md:707 'up to 0.75 s in all'. O-10.txt:84 'drained months-old writes count as fresh'.

title: Escalation buys reasoning, not the missing observation
description: When a failure leaves no trace, the stronger model gets the same empty evidence. The stall log is dots to 96 percent and one watchdog line. The second pytest process is gone. No test encodes the outbox race. Opus or Fable cannot reason past what was never recorded; climbing costs more and returns 'cause unknown'.
evidence: linux-test-runner/task.md:221: 'the log shows no failure, only the stall ... the heartbeat watchdog reports no test id'. HANDOFF:133-134: traced once; the tracing session is not on disk.

title: The cause is in another session's activity
description: The deciding fact sat in what other sessions were doing at that moment: a second pytest process, a machine heavily loaded by other sessions, two checks at once making a slow call look blocked. The failing window cannot see it, so the query cannot carry it, and no entry keyed on this window's symptom can tell the causes apart.
evidence: HANDOFF:132-133 two pytest processes deadlock. linux-test-runner/task.md:221 'heavily loaded by other sessions'. faster-check/task.md:344 'With two checks at once a race test could pass with a broken lock'.

title: An exact symptom match returns a different cause
description: The 9 Nov stall line matches the 5 Nov entry exactly, but that cause (loadfile after a worker crash) was already fixed and no worker died. The design flags a template ambiguous only when two causes are recorded, though the watchdog's own message names three. The outbox's fixed stale-replay entry likewise reads as the answer to the open concurrent race.
evidence: faster-check/task.md:38 'loadfile hangs after the replacement worker starts'; check.py line 85 at bc572f6 'DIST_MODE: Final = "load"'; m1 log line 104 '(a hung test, a worker, or one test longer than that limit)'.

title: A failure that vanishes is never stored
description: The library stores solutions. A stall that passes on rerun, or a chance failure seen once in another session, is never solved, so nothing is written; the design keeps undiagnosed defects out on purpose. The next session meets the same failure with nothing, reruns and moves on. Earlier sightings live only in prose and commit messages.
evidence: 44d115b: 'the S09 test failed twice by chance (once in the cutoff guards session, once on main)'. KS §7.3: 'open defects without a diagnosis stay owned by G2'. task.md:221 'its cause is not known'.

title: The judge was a strong model, and it was half right
description: In each case the wrong answer was caught by a stronger reviewer, not by a test. One Opus review refuted the sequence fixture and, in the same pass, approved a retry delay that still broke the 0.6 s window; the Fable root caught that at gate. The dispatcher's first write-up held two false claims that a review pass found.
evidence: review-opus-round2.md:8 'Fixed: 0.05 s per attempt'; clinic-build/task.md:707 FC-01. HANDOFF:157-166: a CI-red test 'pinned the consent leak'; a guard 'aimed at a statement that cannot raise'.

title: A rule in one project is a bug in the other
description: FixFlow's 'never run two pytest processes against that DB' contradicts the clinic's designed two test slots, and the clinic's mechanism differs (dropped databases, fixed with per-checkout names and a checkout lock). The clinic's transfer note tells FixFlow to audit Hypothesis and hex-tag fixtures FixFlow does not have.
evidence: HANDOFF:132; faster-check/task.md:347 FS-02 'autoclobber lets one drop the other's'; sweep-cards A3-14 'FixFlow's Hypothesis/uuid-based fixtures'; grep of backend/tests: no Hypothesis, no uuid4().hex[: labels.

title: Data-state entries never go stale
description: The cursor entry's truth depends on prod rows: how many events sit above the seed. While the dispatcher stays off, events pile up above the July seed, and drained offline writes land with fresh timestamps that pass the age guard. No footprint item sees prod data, so the entry stays validated while its claim decays.
evidence: KS §5.5: 'Production data state (... the dispatcher cursor row ...), which is not in git.' SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md:102 're-seeded at T_close and again after every P4r'. O-10.txt:84 (O10-F7).

title: Two sessions solved one flake hours apart, one wrongly
description: The root diagnosed the random hex tags at 20:20 UTC. The Sonnet session, on a branch cut before that commit, built and committed a wrong fixture 3 h 46 min later. Under the owner's store-every-solve rule the root's entry would have reached it. Under the design's write trigger a routine test-helper fix is not recorded, so the duplicate would still happen.
evidence: 44d115b (Fable 5.1, 01:20 +0500); 6ac4577 (Sonnet 5.5, 05:06 +0500); 030c6cb 'its diagnosis was wrong'. KS §7.3: 'Routine fixes are not recorded'.

title: Operator hazards are reached only by wording
description: The cursor hazard fires on an operator action, not on code or an error. The design reaches it only through the action handle the writer chose ('enable dispatcher'). The later sessions act under other verbs: drain, restore, re-point, close the window. A different verb is a miss, with no error text to fall back on.
evidence: KS §3.3 line 263: action 'stays the only route for operator-action hazards ... a snapshot restore'. SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md:102 and :723 ('Window close, ceilings, re-seed').

title: Two checked answers did not make a checked merge
description: In every case the composite failed at the seam between lessons that were each right alone. The seam held a fact no parent entry stated: done+offline before the bill is sent (C1b), a rollback after Meta accepted (C2), a same-day import (C3), an unthrottled correct-PIN path (C4). Fetching both parents would not have supplied it.
evidence: da988e2: 'The #163 freeze only catches this once the bill is sent/negotiated/paid.' Handoff §3 item 3: 'B2 resurrected inside the error path that fixes B2.' GC-01 (7f348b2c L10807): 'the stock is in twice.'

title: Failure was seen only by a separate adversarial pass
description: No case gave a failure signal from inside. Suites were green while the composite was wrong. Each fault was found by a red team, a refute-review or a second review pass. The ladder climbs on visible failure, so none would have climbed. Some tests pinned wrong behaviour, or were to be inverted on instruction.
evidence: 4a40423 '594 unit + 131 integration', then 370e83a 'found by an adversarial red-team of #162'. fc119d3 '1980 passed' vs GC-01 'every stock test posts the day after'. Handoff §3: a test 'pinned the consent leak'.

title: The top-tier answer was the wrong one
description: The design stores the top rung's solve and judges cheap output as 'equal' to it. Three times here the top-tier or verified answer was wrong, and the correction came from an adversarial role at the same or a lower tier. There was no single strong answer to be equal to.
evidence: 834311f (Fable 5): 'so enable_dispatcher stays safe to flip' vs handoff B1, B3. Brief by claude-fable-5-1 (7f348b2c L9742) set the stock rule behind GC-01. A2's verified 'Fix' refused by 1c546a3 (Opus 5).

title: Half-right entries would anchor the merge
description: The entries a lookup would return as solved were half-right, and the defect sat inside the stored fix. A cheap model reading them would conclude the door was closed. In C2 the half-right entry came from the top rung and contradicts the prescription it would be shown beside.
evidence: KS L197: '37821f5 incomplete'; da988e2: the prefill's 'catch { return; }'. 0a40416: 'always self-healing'. 834311f: 'never a duplicate' vs handoff B3: 'The claim row is flush-only'.

title: A trade between lessons ends with the owner, not a rung
description: When two lessons conflict, the answer is a policy choice: DoS against brute force, resume against double-send, which meaning of cutoff. The record shows the owner or root choosing, or the choice left open. The ladder Sonnet, Opus, Fable has no rung that can solve a trade once.
evidence: 1c546a3: 'The owner chose to keep the lock'. Handoff §3 item 3: 'The resume-vs-double-send design decision is still open'. GC-01: 'Choose and record: (a) ... or (b)'. task.md:5: 'PROPOSED engineering defaults'.

title: No capture point was solved
description: Each fix of a composite was revised by the next pass. Capturing at any commit stores a rule that the next round changes, or that itself creates new defects. The C3 rule caused three P2s and two P1s; #162 was corrected within hours; c731e66 left its own error path open.
evidence: 370e83a, 9 hours after 4a40423: 'found by an adversarial red-team of #162'. task.md:63: 'three new P2s caused by the end-of-day rule'. Board: 'GD-01 | The RR-2 hold never ends'.

title: The parts are known only after diagnosis
description: The useful earlier lessons were stored in mechanism words from other slices. The later problem arrived in symptom words, or with no symptom at all. A lexical lookup cannot reach a part until the diagnosis has named it, and by then most of the merge is done.
evidence: 4a40423: patterns 'built for money paths and never generalised to lifecycle paths'; symptom 'The job never left ongoing'. 67218b1: 'guarded claim (409)'. B2 found by an audit sweep, with no symptom (handoff §8).

title: Either/or looked like both
description: Two entries partly matched and disagreed. In C3 both define the cutoff, one as end of day and one as count observation; the top rung picked the wrong one. In C4 both entries point at DoS and look complementary, but one removes the throttle the other exists for.
evidence: 97380a1e L1235: 'a cash opening is the account's balance at the end of the cutoff day ... a stock opening is its opening count, observed when the batch posts'. 1c546a3: 'traded a DoS for a much worse brute-force hole'.

title: The answer channel holds two cards
description: KS shows at most one lead and one candidate within 2,000 characters, and has no merge operation. The composites needed four patterns (C1a) or four findings (C2: B1, B2, B3 and the #163 freeze). Even with perfect matching, half the parts would not reach the window.
evidence: KS L304: 'shown: at most one lead and one candidate ... one total output cap of 2,000 characters'. 4a40423 names four patterns. Handoff §7 item 4: 'all of it fires on the same single operator action'.

title: A later fix silently changed an older entry's truth
description: A fix in one slice changed what an older entry in another slice means, with no shared file, so footprint invalidation sees neither side. #163 made bill_sent_at the freeze key; the dispatcher, built three weeks earlier, never stamps it. KS admits 'semantic changes outside the footprint' cannot be detected.
evidence: 834311f (2026-07-08) built the send path. Handoff B2: 'This reopens the exact carry-in loop #162/#163 closed, through the automated path.' b356158: 'a receipt of the medicine (item, then scope) and the opening could deadlock once'.

title: The entries share no node to join on
description: The merge was an analogy across slices: a claim guard reused for lifecycle transitions, a cash cutoff reused for stock. No reasoning step was shared, so there was no branch point to join. KS's only join is a shared root_cause_id, which these entries lack.
evidence: KS L239: 'root_cause_id ... so shares a root cause is a join'. 4a40423: 'transition() never read the current status'. c1fb346: 'a stock opening is the shelf at the end of its cutoff day, as for cash and pay'.

title: The writer could not know which details mattered
description: The strong writer's account left out the detail that later decided the merge. The handoff described one door of four. The dispatcher commit promised claim-before-send without saying the claim was only flushed, which is what B3 turned on.
evidence: da988e2: 'C1 had THREE doors, not the one the handoff described'. 834311f: 'Claim-before-send: a crash leaves a visible pending, never a duplicate.' Handoff B3: 'The claim row is flush-only'.

title: The ladder's order is not who catches the error
description: The ladder assumes a higher tier is more right. Here the wrong conclusions were written or adjudicated at the top (Fable). Corrections came from Opus agents with a different brief or data source, or from the owner, who is above every rung. Escalating by price would hand the problem to the tier that made the error.
evidence: L07-1: claude-fable-5-1 wrote 'a usage limit stopped every session'; Opus 5.5 agent abd913ed9a816c649 found Event 6008. L07-3: an Opus invariants critic caught the Fable-adjudicated v6. L07-2, L07-4 v1.2, L07-6: the owner overturned them.

title: Checks passed conclusions that were wrong
description: With no test, a review is the only check. Every review examined what its brief named and passed the conclusion. Each was then overturned by a different lens or by the owner. A conclusion labelled 'checked' carried no more weight than an unchecked one.
evidence: HB:238 'checked ... by an edge-accuracy check, a refuter and two independent classifiers', then HB:251 'withdrawn'. HR-A1a: judges 'change_now', then critique-5.md:16 [BLOCKER]. KS v1.2: 15 claims refuted, then the owner. L07-6: nine refuters 'narrowed'.

title: Delivered but not applied
description: The right lesson was in the window and was not used. In L07-6 the memory index line was in the first request, and the same mistake came 2.5 hours after the lesson was written. In L07-1 the root's own board recorded unclean PC shutdowns on 5 and 6 Nov, and the root wrote 'usage limit'.
evidence: 0bf1c4f3 record #30 holds '[Test the best form of an idea]'; owner at 12:46Z: 'You're thinking very narrowly'. task.md:832: 'two unclean shutdowns of the PC under concurrent full test runs (5 and 6 November 2026)'.

title: Corrections do not reach copies
description: When a conclusion is corrected, its copies in other documents keep the old text, and new sessions read the copy. The library would hold the correction as a new entry, while the derived records outside it stay wrong.
evidence: task.md:763 still says 'A usage limit stopped every session'. HV2:371 'A graph server needs memory this PC does not have' was refuted at 07:03Z and read intact by 0bf1c4f3 at 10:03Z. PLAYBOOK.md:84 still says 'Supabase GoTrue'.

title: Invalidation has nothing to watch
description: A research or design conclusion rests on premises outside git: an event log, free memory on the PC, the owner's standard, or code not yet written. KS invalidates by file footprint and doc_ref only, so the facts that overturned these conclusions could never fire it.
evidence: Event 6008 (L07-1); '7-12 GB is free' (L07-2); the GoTrue plan had no footprint before 30dc6d4 wrote identity/ another way (L07-5); KS §5.5 lists untracked dependencies as undetectable.

title: The conclusion answers its own day's question
description: A stored conclusion was fetched for a later question that shares its words but not its goal, and it framed the answer. The owner rejected the result each time the goal had moved.
evidence: L07-2: a code-graph token verdict met 'graphs where branches can be merged'. L07-4: a defect-store design priced a cross-project reasoning library. L07-5: the 'GoTrue' plan met a name + PIN roster.

title: A top-model guess is stored as a finding
description: The strong model stated an unchecked assumption in the same voice as a checked fact. Capture of 'the strong model's conclusion' cannot tell them apart. The KS write rule would exclude the guess, but it would exclude the correction too.
evidence: Root, 9 Nov 12:03:46Z: 'halted ... Docker down'; 12:04:19Z: 'a usage limit stopped every session', with no limit check between. e24f17dc #7043: 'A graph database server would need memory this PC does not have free'; refuter: '7-12 GB is free'.

title: The query carries the hypothesis
description: The words of a later brief come from the stored framing, so a lookup selects the entry that holds the error and confirms it. The right lead shares few words with the query.
evidence: Owner's B03 and card A8-06 say 'usage limit halted'. The board's 'unclean shutdown of 6 November 2026' (task.md:588) shares only the date. 'Graph' matched code-graph verdicts for a retrieval question (L07-2).

title: Checks built from the conclusion share its blind spot
description: The gates and metrics that would check reuse were written from the same conclusion, so they accept its failure mode. Reusing the entry passes its own checks.
evidence: critique-5.md:16: 'P5c's indoor test accepts server verdict inside or unknown ... so no gate catches the loss'. KS §12.7 point 0: the fallback rate 'counted the visible failure and not a silently wrong span'.

title: A stored 'no' is read as 'never'
description: A conditional prohibition lost its condition when copied. Later work obeyed it after the condition was met. A do-not-build line also outlived the test it came from.
evidence: 6928828: 're-add the plugin only once a Sentry project + auth token exist'. 140428c: CLAUDE.md 'must never be added'. a31924a obeyed it with project 4511846063013968 live. HB:263 kept 'do not build: a graph database server' after HB:251.

title: The solved moment is unclear, and capture can hold the wrong version
description: A design looks final when committed and is overturned minutes or days later. The commit that marks it can also hold an older text than its message says.
evidence: 3fb8f9c (21:27:58) v6 ruling; 4e01c82 (21:50:48) blocker fixed. 46c5d98: 'commit 093b793 still carried v3 by mistake'. KS v1.2, v1.3, v1.3.1 within two days.

title: Partial matches contradict each other
description: One lookup returns several conclusions on one topic, in different states: withdrawn, narrowed, refuted but unchanged, skipped, pending. Nothing tells the cheap model which one governs. Only explicit supersession links them, and these were separate entries.
evidence: For 'graph' on 12 Nov: HB:247 withdrawn, HB:263 narrowed, HV2:371 refuted but unchanged, KS §1.4 'graphify ... skipped', graph2/protocol.md frozen and not run.

title: Nothing fires: the needed lessons are about acts that raise no error
description: KS lookups fire before escalating, before retrying a build or deploy, before a prescribed fix, on a gate error, and on --diff. Every act that needed a cross-project lesson was off that list: a research clone, a brief, a session start, a decision to accept a handicap, a long command. Three raised no error at all. The owner was the trigger twice.
evidence: 7f348b2c L955 start_session no model, L995 owner 'you started it with fable 5.1??'; e24f17dc L7539 plans a handicap, L7543 owner 'run a linux machiune'; brief 'Put a full report.md there'.

title: The design has no cross-project path
description: KS is one store for FixFlow (.fixflow-ks), seeded only from FixFlow, with repo-relative handles, controls on FixFlow mainline shas, an existence filter that demotes entries whose paths are absent, and its CLI in FixFlow's tools/ks. The clinic has no CLI. Every clinic-to-FixFlow transfer here is a miss by construction; the owner's 'across projects' goal has no mechanism.
evidence: KS §4.1 step 2 existence filter; §3.4 controls are FixFlow 40-hex shas; F1-ks-mechanics §9 'The design says nothing about reuse across projects'. No FixFlow record cites clinic 9982012 or 5816c70.

title: The top tier lacked the knowledge; the ladder has nowhere to go
description: The library aims at cheap models and climbs to Fable on failure. In every case the window missing the cross-project fact was Fable itself, the orchestrator. In L08-3 the failure was overspend, which produces correct output, so no rung or check sees it.
evidence: c1797e48 claude-fable-5-1 at ~196k; 7f348b2c claude-fable-5-1 at ~460k; e24f17dc claude-fable-5-2 at ~380k (L7533) and the Fable-written 11-12 briefs.

title: A correction at the wrong scope overturned a right entry and spread
description: The clinic refusal was a real harness error on analysis-*.md, while Sonnet agents of the same type wrote other .md files. FixFlow's probe wrote a .txt and declared 'They can'. A remedy and briefs were built on it, and 8 of 8 report.md writes were refused the next day. The record still says 'They can'.
evidence: cb58bdc7 a8f87cc L257 'Subagents should return findings as text, not write report files'; machine-facts.md:33 probe .txt; e24f17dc wf_548351eb/wf_5a9f904a 8 refusals, 187,160 chars; HARNESS-BOTTLENECKS:23 unchanged after 08:07Z.

title: Machine and harness facts have no gate
description: Path length, harness write policy, session tier, Windows DLLs and shell length cannot be read by any KS check kind (git blobs, repo tests, db probe), and none has a fails_at/passes_at commit pair. They are capped at candidate, the CLI withholds the fix because only 'applies' prints it, and the write gate's control pair cannot be made.
evidence: KS §4.1 step 5 'Only applies lets ks show print the fix'; §3.4 check kinds; L08-1 DLL cause is the 208-char clone root, not a commit (development-guide.md:28).

title: In the window is not in use
description: Delivery had already happened and the rule was still not applied when the matching act came. The Explore-inherits rule sat at line 3 of a 460k window during three no-model starts. The 8 KB rule's own author sent an 8,720-char command 25 hours later. The Linux-container fact was in the session's own compile.
evidence: 7f348b2c L3 paste vs L667/L732/L955; reference-bash-tool-limits.md (11-11 07:05Z) vs e24f17dc L7359 8,720 chars, L7367 'unexpected EOF'; HARNESS-BOTTLENECKS:65 vs L7539.

title: Similar is not the same across projects
description: The stored fix did not fit the new act even where the principle did: an Explore subagent pinned to Haiku vs start_session parameters; a speed move to Linux vs a missing native library; two different 'Filename too long' templates. What carried over was a principle or a permission, not a solution.
evidence: fixflow-explorer.md:3 vs 7f348b2c L1018; use-the-machine-parallelism.md (latency) vs e24f17dc L7491 arrow.dll/networkit_state.dll; dfe1ea6e L697 vs c1797e48 L227.

title: The writer saw a paraphrase, not the raw error
description: The harness string that names 'report files' (the best key and the discriminator) stayed in subagent transcripts. The root saw only the agent's paraphrase and stored a guess about agent type or size. The shell errors were stored as 'failed a long Bash heredoc'. KS forbids extracting from transcripts.
evidence: cb58bdc7 L360 'The harness blocks subagents from writing report files'; subagents-return-text-not-files.md:15 'may depend on the agent type or output size'; a6a48ae L186 EOF error not stored.

title: A stored 'no' read as 'never'; two projects' rules collide
description: FixFlow's 'nothing may be installed without an owner decision' produced a recorded handicap until the owner overrode it, while the clinic already had owner approval for Linux containers (USER-23). The clinic's 'nothing inherits the root's model' meets FixFlow's Fable-orchestrated starts. Which project's rule holds is not in the entry.
evidence: e24f17dc L7245 'Nothing new may be installed without the owner's decision, so do not install anything'; L7543 owner override; orchestration.md:14 vs FixFlow 7 of 7 starts with no model.

title: Pull-only gives up the prevention the push index gave
description: The MEMORY.md index put the longpaths fix in sibling session 9c3f9742's window before its first clone, and that clone never failed. The clinic guide did the same for five later sessions. A lookup fired by failure always pays the first failure in each new session or project.
evidence: 9c3f9742 L16 index line (07:17Z), L240 first clone already uses 'git -c core.longpaths=true'; clinic sessions vigilant-chatelet L156, ecstatic-snyder L196 read development-guide.md:28 at start.

title: One entry holds several facts of different scope
description: The clinic tier note mixes a tier rule, a harness rule (start_session refused on automated turns), a clinic test-database collision and two owner exceptions. The subagent-write note hides the shell-length fact. A hit returns foreign scope or the wrong fact.
evidence: tiered-model-orchestration.md (Harness rule 2026-11-03; Gate mechanics test_clinic_sNN; Exception precedent); subagents-return-text-not-files.md:11 'one also failed a long Bash heredoc'.

title: Each project stores only the half it saw
description: FixFlow's longpaths note has the git half and not the clinic's DLL half. FixFlow's B16 correction dropped the clinic's scope (Opus agents, analysis files, Sonnet wrote fine). Each writer knew only its own episode.
evidence: project-windows-git-longpaths.md (git only) vs development-guide.md:28 (DLL); HARNESS-BOTTLENECKS:49 'two agents' unchecked report' vs cb58bdc7 a1db83e L265 Sonnet write ok.

title: Equal to the strong model copies the strong model's errors
description: The goal is output equal to the strong model's. In every case a top-tier model made or endorsed the error: Opus slice authors and the Fable root (lock attribution), an Opus-high session with two Opus reviews (reversal test), the Fable root widening and a Fable compile flipping the subagent rule, an Opus-high critic and map lanes (34 minutes). Equality would reproduce these.
evidence: Slice sessions Opus (a9b52f2e 835 calls, 1c7937a3 857); root 7f348b2c Fable. 'the root's own round-1 premise was wrong' (task.md:303). Critic model: 'opus', effort: 'high' (sweep wf:91).

title: Role, access and execution caught errors; tier did not
description: No error was settled by moving up a tier. Catches came from a same-tier reviewer with a refute brief, the test runner on the merged tree, a same-tier refuter reading a raw transcript, and a tool's own error text. Going up made it worse twice: the Fable root's S04 premise, and the Fable compile siding with a Haiku probe.
evidence: Merged-tree check 'failed 2 of 2570' (task.md:821); refuter and critic both opus/high; Haiku probe (e24f17dc 00:33Z) overrode Opus analysts' refused writes (cb58bdc7 subagents).

title: Nothing fails, so nothing triggers
description: The defects were a test that passes, a full check that passes, and a confident 'not found'. A cheap model doing these tasks gets no signal that it needs help, so neither a lookup nor the ladder starts.
evidence: 'pass with those locks removed' (task.md:149); 'record the full check (2570 passed)' (6eaed2a); 'CONFIRMED NOT FOUND' (sweep-critic.txt:4).

title: A correction is an entry too, tested under a different condition
description: Three times a later, stronger-looking check overrode a claim that was right, by testing something else. G04-02 moved the slice's correct ISS-counter attribution to the scope lock. A one-line .txt probe 'refuted' a report-file refusal. A task.md search 'refuted' the owner's 34 minutes. Nothing records which condition each side tested.
evidence: Y2 reversed G04-02 (task.md:303); probe 'subagent-write-probe.txt' vs refused 'analysis-ai-ux.md'; refute.txt:33 'the owner's figure is wrong' vs 'waited 2030 s'.

title: Same claim, different cause; delivered lesson followed in form
description: From S04 every slice brief carried the race-test lesson; each slice ran experiments and failed a new way (helper timing, earlier code variant, wrong layer, no load-bearing lock). One entry would surface for all and be right for one. S02 V1 (rows) and the reversal test (schema) are one class with different mechanisms.
evidence: S04 brief 'record a lock-removal experiment for each, as S02 and S03 did' (a9b52f2e); 'experiments were unsound' (review-round-1.md:11); 'E6 was an earlier code variant' (task.md:411).

title: A passing check certifies a latent defect; reuse multiplies it
description: The pay follow-up's reversal test passed its gate on 6 Nov and became the template. The real-data session copied it into two new tests. It failed only once migration 0015 existed, and only in some test orders. Race tests likewise pass whichever guard happens to decide; adding a guard changes the answer silently.
evidence: 6a2fd45: 'The two new reversal tests get the same change'; branch 2570 passed, merged 2 of 2570 failed; check-summary.md:75 item lock or unique rule decides when locks go.

title: The deciding detail is dropped when an entry is written or copied
description: The scope that made each claim true was lost one copy later. 'Report files' became 'file writes from subagents are refused'. 'Not in docs/tasks/*/task.md' became 'in no file'. The writer did not know which word mattered.
evidence: Memory: 'cannot write report files'; orchestration.md:14 'file writes from subagents are refused here'; sweep-critic.txt:9 'any docs/tasks/*/task.md' vs map-full.txt:255 'appears in no file'.

title: Copies of a refuted entry survive
description: Corrections reached the top document but not every copy. A trial's stop rule still uses 742 s. The clinic's orchestration doc still carries the widened rule. The compile still carries the wrong correction after fresh refusals.
evidence: verdicts.txt:30 'a slot wait over 742 s, the largest recorded'; orchestration.md:14 unchanged since 5816c70; HARNESS-BOTTLENECKS:23 'They can.' saved 08:07Z on 12 Nov.

title: The needed knowledge was an observation, not a solved problem
description: What later sessions needed was a measured fact: a 2030 s wait, a harness refusal of report files. Nobody solved anything, so a library that stores solutions and their reasoning never captures it. The truth sat in tool output inside transcripts.
evidence: 7f348b2c 2026-11-09T12:52:03Z 'waited 2030 s'; refusal text in cb58bdc7 subagents; KS entry kinds defect, trap, do_not_apply, open_defect, rule_without_case (L239).

title: Contrary evidence stays inside subagent windows
description: On 12 Nov eight subagents met the refusal that the session's compile said did not exist. Each adapted and returned structured output. The root never saw the tool errors and saved the compile later that day unchanged. Evidence against an entry is met where it cannot reach the entry's writer.
evidence: e24f17dc workflows wf_548351eb-ab1, wf_5a9f904a-4b0: report.md refused 06:56:45Z-07:43:46Z (4 Opus, 4 Sonnet); HARNESS-BOTTLENECKS saved 08:07Z.

title: A stored 'not found' overrules the person who was right
description: The critic's scoped negative became 'the owner's figure is wrong' and a stop rule. The owner had the right number; so did the clinic root's own recap three days earlier.
evidence: refute.txt:33 ''34 minutes' appears in no file; the owner's figure is wrong'; 7f348b2c recap 'That check waited 34 minutes' (2026-11-09T12:52:45Z).

title: Write rule keyed on solver difficulty skips the cheap model's mistake
description: An Opus session made the reversal-test mistake; the Fable root fixed it in one attempt in about a minute. Under KS's write rule (tier escalation, two failed approaches, or a burned build) that fix is routine and unrecorded. The project's conventions file recorded it anyway.
evidence: Root edits 00:34:08-00:34:12Z after failure at 00:33:14Z (7f348b2c); KS L452 'Routine fixes are not recorded'; conventions line in f6b5c6c.

title: World-state facts change with no event
description: Facts outside the repo changed with nothing in git: a Sentry project now exists, production went dark, uv and Python 3.13 were installed. KS invalidates only on footprint events and has no TTL, so such entries stay as written. Its guard for ex8, an unprobeable precondition capping the verdict at inconclusive, also leaves the entry inconclusive on the day it was right.
evidence: KS §5.1 'No TTL, no review dates'; §5.5 'Production data state ... not in git'; KS L793 'the Sentry project now exists (PR #176)'; CLAUDE.md:36 unchanged since 08-02; uv WinGet folder dated 2026-11-02 22:06, before the 11-04 notes.

title: A copied lesson loses its condition
description: When a lesson is re-written into another library, its scope falls off. 'Re-add only once a Sentry project + auth token exist' became CLAUDE.md's 'must never be added'. 'Not on PATH' became 'no Python on the machine'. Readers then obey the unconditional form: #176 kept the plugin out with a Sentry project live.
evidence: 6928828: 're-add the plugin only once a Sentry project + auth token exist'; 140428c: 'must never be added to app.json'; house-expenses-receipts-program.md:16: 'no Python on the machine'; a31924a: 'stays OUT of app.json'.

title: The solver's write-up misstates what happened, and it spreads
description: After-the-fact write-ups were wrong and the errors travelled. 6928828 says the plugin re-entered main via #59; the removal never reached main, and R-02 then counted the trap 'hit twice'. The truth-pass claim was false 86 minutes after the contradicting code landed. 093b793's subject names a version the commit never wrote.
evidence: a6f9048 is not an ancestor of main; b4f0766 merged at 11:50, the fix came at 16:04; KS L139 'ex8 hit twice in 16 days (added once...)'; the 85c88c0 tree has client_id=uuid4() in record_media_orphan; 46c5d98.

title: The higher-ranked library keeps a line its own audit refuted
description: CLAUDE.md is ranked above every prose doc, by itself and by the HANDOFF. The HANDOFF's audit named a CLAUDE.md line false. Five days later an Opus 5 session working from that HANDOFF rewrote the line and put the media-orphan-sweep row under it. It still stands on 11-12. KS corrects contradictions once, at seeding, and has no path for later ones.
evidence: HANDOFF §4.5 item 1; da988e2 diff: '+... Each job is idempotent, so a duplicate run is harmless.' and '+| `media-orphan-sweep`'; its body: 'Closes C1 and C2 from the 2026-07-28 handoff'; KS §8 rule 5.

title: No trigger on build or documentation work
description: The hazards arrived inside ordinary tasks: wiring a DSN, and restructuring CLAUDE.md. Neither raised a failure or an escalation. The design's remaining route, --diff, joins only code and config lines. So the CLAUDE.md rewrite was invisible to it, and on 07-18 no entry yet covered empty env values.
evidence: 140428c ('empty = off'; every eas build failed until 79a8dd4); the da988e2 CLAUDE.md rewrite (338 lines); KS §7.2 join over 'code and config files only'.

title: Only an expensive adversarial pass checks the library's own entries
description: Nothing checked prose claims by use. The false idempotency line stood 20 days, until an audit with a REFUTED default found it. The wrong 'hit twice' history of the Sentry trap was caught only by a refuter. Both checks were top-tier sessions run on purpose.
evidence: HANDOFF header: 'survived an adversarial verifier whose default verdict was REFUTED'; KS L139 lists R-02 claims that verification 'narrowed or withdrew'; L503: 'R-02 says the Sentry plugin was "re-added twice"'.

title: A lookup costs a turn when the push library already delivered
description: When CLAUDE.md or MEMORY.md already carries the lesson, a pull lookup adds a turn and saves nothing. On 08-03 the agent obeyed both CLAUDE.md traps, yet --diff would still raise the ex7 warning for a reviewer ruling. On 11-09 and 11-12 the note's remedy was already in the command that hit the error.
evidence: a31924a: 'Two traps this deliberately respects, both documented in CLAUDE.md'; agent-a24b85dfbf353e137.jsonl:39 '|| node -e'; agent-a134a5fb8402fd8bf.jsonl:56.

title: An error line is not a failure
description: All three 'Python was not found' errors after the note came from hedged probes that carried the note's remedy in the same command, at no extra cost. A failure detector, ladder trigger or missed-lookup count keyed on error text would score the library's successes as misses. The 11-12 refuter's post-note list counts them as re-hits.
evidence: agent-a7d5404af4b1e0cff.jsonl:37: 'python3 -c "print(1)" ...; P=<codex path>; "$P" -c'; agent-a134a5fb8402fd8bf.jsonl:56-57; refuter list at wf_b516f6cc agent-a1e89191a0c75a205.jsonl:158.

title: One symptom, two causes; the entry fits one
description: Build 15 had two causes under one generic Gradle code: the stranded plugin, and Dependabot's SDK-56 pins. A stored entry covers the first. Its probe would pass after the fix while the build still failed, and nothing in the result says a second cause exists.
evidence: 6928828: 'Two root causes'; KS §3.3 flags EAS_BUILD_UNKNOWN_GRADLE_ERROR, 'which build 15 had two causes for'; KS §9 limit 4: the gate proves a condition, not a cause.

title: The first time is full price
description: The empty-string DSN had no entry before 07-18, and the first agent to try it broke every EAS build for two days. ex7 exists only because of that failure.
evidence: 140428c: 'wire Sentry DSN plumbing through eas.json (empty = off)'; 79a8dd4: 'every `eas build` failed schema validation before it started'.

title: Parallel windows each pay before any entry exists
description: One workflow started 133 subagent windows. 86 hit the same missing-Python error within 22 minutes, and 17 repeated it in their next call. An entry written after the first failure reaches none of the siblings already running. Under pull, each window also fails once before it can look anything up.
evidence: House-expenses session 4f9060c4, wf_1cc608d4-f56: 86 tool results from 2026-11-03T19:16:34Z to 19:38:53Z; next calls: PowerShell 34, node 20, python 17.

title: Same fact, different truth per project
description: The machine's Python is recorded five ways in three projects. 'uv run python' works only in the clinic's venv, 'use node' is EMS advice, and 'no Python on the machine' is false everywhere. A cross-project match returns entries that are each right only in their own scope. KS does not cover other projects at all.
evidence: clinic-s00-readiness-2026-11.md:13 'no uv'; project-windows-git-longpaths.md 'use `node` for JSON'; house-expenses-receipts-program.md:16; F1 §9: 'The design says nothing about reuse across projects'.
